questions.question: What is 'fan-out on write' in a social media feed system?
options: Querying all followed users' posts when a user opens their feed
Pre-computing each follower's feed by pushing new posts into their cache at write time
Writing posts to multiple database replicas for durability
Sending push notifications to all followers when a post is created
questions.explanation: Fan-out on write means that when a user creates a post, the system immediately pushes that post into the pre-computed feed cache of every follower. This makes feed reads extremely fast — just read from cache.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of fan-out on read over fan-out on write?
options: Faster feed loading times for users
Lower write amplification — no need to update millions of caches when a user posts
Better message ordering in the feed
Simpler database schema design
questions.explanation: Fan-out on read avoids the write amplification problem. A single post doesn't trigger millions of cache updates. Instead, the feed is assembled at read time by querying followed users' posts. The trade-off is higher read latency.

questions.question: What is the 'celebrity problem' in feed design?
options: Celebrities post too frequently and flood the system
Users with millions of followers make fan-out on write extremely expensive
Celebrity content gets more engagement, skewing ranking algorithms
Celebrities require special authentication and security measures
questions.explanation: A celebrity with millions of followers would require millions of cache updates for a single post using fan-out on write. This is prohibitively expensive, so systems use a hybrid approach where celebrity posts use fan-out on read instead.

questions.question: How does a hybrid fan-out approach handle the celebrity problem?
options: All posts use fan-out on read to keep things simple
Regular users fan-out on write; celebrities fan-out on read; the timeline service merges both at read time
Celebrity posts are delayed by 5 minutes to spread the load
Celebrities are limited to one post per hour
questions.explanation: The hybrid approach uses fan-out on write for regular users (fast reads from cache) and fan-out on read for celebrities (avoiding massive write amplification). The timeline service merges the cached feed with celebrity posts at read time.

questions.question: Why do feed caches typically store only post IDs rather than full post content?
options: Post IDs are encrypted while full content is not
Storing IDs reduces cache size and allows post content to be updated independently without invalidating feeds
Post IDs are faster to sort than full content
Full post content cannot be stored in Redis
questions.explanation: Storing only post IDs in the feed cache minimizes memory usage (IDs are tiny compared to full posts with images and metadata). It also means that if a post is edited or its like count changes, the feed cache doesn't need to be updated — the post service returns fresh content when hydrating.

questions.question: What data structure is commonly used to detect trending topics in real-time with bounded memory?
options: A hash map storing exact counts for every hashtag
A count-min sketch that approximates frequency counts in constant space
A binary search tree sorted by hashtag popularity
A relational database table with hashtag counts
questions.explanation: A count-min sketch is a probabilistic data structure that approximates the frequency of items (like hashtags) using constant memory. It may overcount but never undercount, making it ideal for detecting trending topics in high-volume streams.

questions.question: How does a modern feed ranking system differ from a purely chronological feed?
options: Ranking systems display posts in random order
Ranking systems score posts by relevance signals like engagement, relationship closeness, and content type
Ranking systems only show posts from verified accounts
Ranking systems delay all posts by one hour for content review
questions.explanation: Modern feed ranking uses ML models that score posts based on signals like predicted engagement (likes, comments, shares), how close the viewer is to the poster, content type preferences, and recency. The goal is to maximize user engagement.

questions.question: A user follows 500 accounts. With fan-out on read, how many queries are needed to assemble their feed?
options: 1 query to a single feed cache
Up to 500 queries (one per followed account) plus a merge operation
Exactly 10 queries using pagination
2 queries: one for posts and one for engagement data
questions.explanation: Fan-out on read requires fetching recent posts from each followed account — potentially 500 queries that must be merged and sorted. This is why fan-out on read has higher read latency, and why systems prefer fan-out on write for regular users.

questions.question: A celebrity with 50 million followers posts a tweet using fan-out on write. Each cache update takes 0.01ms. How long does the full fan-out take on a single machine?
options: 0.5 seconds
5 seconds
500 seconds (over 8 minutes)
5000 seconds (over 83 minutes)
questions.explanation: 50 million updates at 0.01ms each = 500,000ms = 500 seconds, or about 8.3 minutes. Even distributed across 100 workers, it would take 5 seconds. This illustrates exactly why fan-out on write is impractical for celebrities.

questions.question: In a hybrid feed system, a user follows 300 regular users and 5 celebrities. At feed load time, what operations does the timeline service perform?
options: It queries all 305 accounts' posts and merges them
It reads the pre-computed cache (containing 300 regular users' posts), fetches the 5 celebrities' recent posts, merges and ranks them
It only shows celebrity posts since they have higher engagement
It queries the 300 regular users and ignores celebrity posts until scrolling
questions.explanation: The timeline service reads the user's pre-computed feed cache (already containing posts from 300 regular users pushed via fan-out on write), then fetches recent posts from the 5 celebrities (fan-out on read), merges both sets, applies ranking, and returns the final feed.
